final_answer:
PLAN DEVIATION REPORT - In re Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc., No. 25-30412-MLE (Bankr. D. Or.)
Compares Committee redline to the Debtor's filed Plan (4/28/25) using the Clearview summary, DS excerpts and the 5/19/25 transmittal. Cites are to the FILED Plan unless "Redline".

1. BOTTOM LINE
(a) The redline is not a true compare against the filed Plan. Its base text differs from the filed Plan (article/section numbers, class numbers, Exhibit C contents, Released Parties, trustee selection, conditions). The "47 changes / 15 cosmetic" label cannot be relied on; at least six "cosmetic" or "correction" items are substantive. Demand a machine compare against the filed Plan before any section-by-section negotiation.
(b) The equity "arithmetic error" is a negotiated allocation (Plan 4.3, DS 9.1) that Clearview's math shows over-compensates Timberline; the Committee is right on direction but its 41.07% fix is flawed.
(c) The Committee's cash asks fail the Debtor's feasibility and Effective Date cash condition on the current numbers.
(d) The email understates scope: the avoidance-action and release changes reach far beyond the $9.5M preference pool.

2. REDLINE INTEGRITY PROBLEMS (not disclosed in the email)
- Numbering: Redline places releases in Art. VIII, contracts in Art. VII, GUCs in "Class 3". Filed Plan: releases Art. X (10.4/10.5), contracts Art. VIII, GUCs Class 4, Timberline Class 3. DS uses yet another scheme (GUC Class 6, Timberline Class 5). Redline "8.2(b)" strike corresponds to filed 10.4(c); "6.4/6.6" retention = filed 5.8; "6.5" board = 5.4; "6.7" trust = 5.9; "9.1(g)" falls in a conditions article structured differently from filed 9.1/9.2. Changes cannot be accepted mechanically and some may attach to text the Debtor never filed.
- Released Parties: Redline base omits Timberline and First Meridian; filed 10.4(a)(iii)-(iv) includes both. The Timberline "carve-out" is drafted against a definition that differs from ours.
- Litigation Trustee: Redline base says selected by "Debtor"; filed 5.9(b) says Reorganized Debtor with Committee consent (DS says Debtor with Committee consent).
- Effective Date: Change #7 is labeled "clause numbering" but rewrites the definition (redline: first Business Day after conditions; filed: 30 days after Final Order plus 9.2 conditions) and adds a cash-sufficiency condition. Redline's separate "9.1(g)" waiver veto is in the same cluster.
- Exhibit C: The redline's schedule is not the filed one. Filed rejected list: PacWest, Northshore, Timberpoint, Clearwater Fleet, Rogue Valley Printing ($180,000), Cascaede Janitorial. Redline lists Redmond, High Desert, Deschutes River Environmental ($180,000 to $108,000), Summit. Redline "corrects" typos ("Olypmnic", "Industiral") that do not appear in the filed Plan, and misses the filed typos ("Febuary", "Cascaede"). The Olympic date change (March 15, 2019 to 2020) touches the $22M/yr assumed Centralia supply agreement (filed Ex. C item 1, dated 3/15/2019). Do not accept; verify against the contract and Claim No. 147 (wrong date risks misidentifying the assumed contract and cure). The Deschutes River $180k/$108k change appears to refer to a contract not on the filed schedule; verify Claim No. 203 and amendment of 11/1/2023.

3. SUBSTANTIVE DEVIATIONS (item, filed vs. redline, assessment)

A. GUC pool: $18.7M (10.0%) to $28.0M (14.97%; $28M/$187M correct). Firm per Committee. Effect: Effective Date pool payment $21.0M vs $9.35M.
B. Timing/interest: 50/50 to 75/25 plus interest at the 28 U.S.C. 1961 rate "currently 5.24%". 1961 rate is the weekly average 1-year Treasury yield; published tables show 4.00% for July 2025, so 5.24% appears stale/incorrect. On $7.0M, interest at 5.24% is about $367k. Filed 4.4 says no interest. Negotiable per Committee.
C. Feasibility impact (Clearview Sec. VI; Plan Ex. B; DS 9.2). Cash at emergence $68.0M. Debtor's Effective Date uses $62.85M, cushion $5.15M. Under redline: $12.5M + $3.2M + $2.8M + $35.0M + $21.0M = $74.5M, a $6.5M shortfall. This fails filed 9.2(e) (sufficient Cash) and 1129(a)(11) unless exit financing or other sources are shown. Unmodeled draws: DIP payoff/roll-up (up to $40M; DS 6.4(d) condition, omitted from DS 9.2 table), cure (~$515k), $500k trust funding, fee escrow. Year-1 deferred payment: $7.0M plus interest (~$7.37M) vs. projected Year-1 FCF $8.3M; opening cushion would be negative. Filed 5.2 says Timberline funds the $35M while 4.3(a) says it receives $35M; the $68M apparently includes it. Clean up.
D. Avoidance: Filed 5.9(d): net proceeds retained by Reorganized Debtor. Redline: 100% of net Avoidance Action proceeds to GUCs, additional to the pool. Email frames this as $9.5M preferences, but the definition covers 544/548/550 claims, sweeping any Dividend Recap recovery. Redline text computes 20.05% total recovery on GROSS $9.5M while its comment estimates net $6.0M-$7.5M (3.2%-4.0%). Clearview excludes avoidance from TEV and leaves allocation to the Plan. Trade against the $28M pool. Filed 10.5 already limits retained Avoidance Actions to preferences against non-Released Parties.
E. Equity: Filed 55%/45% (4.3(b), 5.3); Redline 41.07%/58.93%. Facts: TEV $407.5M less $261.4M = $146.1M; $60M/$146.1M = 41.07% (Clearview Step 5). At 55%, Timberline gets $80.355M equity plus $35M cash = $115.355M on a $95M claim (121.4%), an excess of $20.355M (DS 9.1 itself prints these figures). A senior creditor receiving more than 100% is a fair-and-equitable problem under 1129(b)(1)-(2) in any cramdown of Class 4 and a best-interests/good-faith (1129(a)(3)) problem. So the Committee has substance. But: (i) it is a negotiated allocation, not a typo (Plan 4.3 calls 55% "agreed value exchange"), so the Debtor should not "confirm it as a correction"; (ii) 41.07% remains "subject to dilution by the MIP": at 7% MIP Timberline holds about 38.2% (about $55.8M), at 10% about 37.0% ($54.0M), below its $60M; Timberline will object, so draft "fully diluted" basis; (iii) neither Plan nor redline says who owns the remaining 45% or 58.93%. Unissued treasury shares make Timberline the sole outstanding holder (less MIP) and capture the whole $146.1M. At 58.93% the problem worsens. (iv) Clearview's percentage is an illustrative framework (TEV minus senior debt, no cash adjustment), not a fairness opinion. (v) The Committee cites Clearview pp. 8-9; Clearview's report is restricted to Debtor/counsel/FA and marked FRE 408; determine how the Committee obtained it and whether DS Exhibit A makes it public.
F. MIP 10% to 7%: benefits Timberline/treasury holders, not GUCs (who get no equity). Negotiable; ask for market data.
G. Retention bonuses ($3.4M, 12 employees): Filed 5.8 assumes obligations; DS says paid in cash at or promptly after the Effective Date, yet the $3.4M is missing from the Effective Date uses table (cushion falls to $1.75M if paid then). Redline strikes it and adds "11.9". Sec. 503(c)(1) bars retention payments to insiders unless the court finds a bona fide competing offer at equal or greater pay, services essential to survival, and a cap (10x the mean of non-management retention payments; if none, a 25% of prior-year-bonus test). Officers (COO, CFO) are insiders under 101(31)(B). Debtor faces real risk: board approved prepetition, no motion, no evidence of competing offers (DS asserts "recruitment efforts" only). Courts differ on whether 503(c) governs post-effective assumption, but 1129(a)(4) and (a)(5)(B) apply regardless. Recommend a separate 503(c)(3)/KEIP-style motion or restructuring as performance-based incentive for insiders, with non-insider bonuses under 503(c)(3).
H. New Section 11.9 (cramdown): Imposes burden of proof on Debtor "by a preponderance," states retention bonuses "may be characterized" as property retained by junior insiders, and requires Debtor to "address" MIP. Largely a litigation position piece: the Code already places the burden on the proponent, and absolute priority (1129(b)(2)(B)(ii)) concerns junior claims/interests receiving property "on account of" them; employee compensation for post-emergence services is not on account of an equity interest unless recipients hold old equity (Whitaker family 40% and institutions per DS 3.2 are old equity; management status unknown; check). Committee cites Jevic for the absolute priority rule; Jevic (580 U.S. 451 (2017)) concerned priority-skipping structured dismissals; the redline's pin (455) is off. Reject as drafted; offer limited acknowledgment of 1129(b).
I. Contract rejection (filed 8.2; redline 7.2): "business judgment" to "reasonable determination that continued performance would impose a material net burden". Not a minor edit; departs from the settled 365(a) business judgment standard (Ninth Cir.: Pomona Valley Med. Group, 476 F.3d 665 (9th Cir. 2007) - verify). 
J. Board 3-1-1 to 2-2-1: tradeable.
K. Litigation Trustee: Redline gives Committee selection with Debtor consent, versus filed Reorganized Debtor with Committee consent. Plausible given conflicts; paired with 100% proceeds to GUCs. Trust funding is only $500k (filed 5.9(a)).
L. Dividend Recap (Sept. 14, 2021): Redline carves it out of 8.1/8.2(a), the injunction, discharge (redline 10.3) and transfers claims to the Trust; adds condition precedent 9.1(g) (supplemental disclosure, court approved, waivable only with Committee consent) and a Plan Supplement contents addition. Filed 10.4(d) affirmatively releases recap claims and falsely recites that "the Debtor and the Committee have reviewed ... and concluded" the releases are appropriate; the redline does not strike that recital; demand deletion. Facts to correct in negotiations: DS 3.3 shows Timberline was the LENDER ($95M second lien notes), and the ~$88M dividend went to old equity holders (Whitaker family and institutions), not to Timberline (unless affiliated holders exist; the Committee must plead that). DS 3.3 is longer than the "two-sentence" mention the Committee asserts, but it does not address avoidability or release impact. Claim timing: 548 reaches only transfers within two years before the petition (here March 3, 2023); the Sept. 2021 transaction is outside it, so the Committee's "548" theory fails, leaving 544(b) with Oregon UVTA (ORS ch. 95; four-year period, verify ORS 95.280) and 546(a)/108(a) timing, actual-intent theories, equitable subordination (510(c)) or recharacterization of Timberline's notes, and claims against the dividend recipients and officers/directors (who are Released Parties). A solvency opinion supported the deal (DS 3.3). Condition 9.1(g) gives the Committee a veto and a timing lever (DS hearing June 12; confirmation July 24; effective Aug. 15), and the "Committee's position" element requires the Debtor to publish the opposing view.
M. Third-party releases: Filed 10.4 mixes consensual and "non-consensual" (opt-out) releases; DS 6.3 expressly calls them non-consensual. Harrington v. Purdue Pharma L.P., 603 U.S. 204 (2024), holds the Code does not authorize nonconsensual third-party releases; Ninth Circuit already barred them under 524(e) (Resorts Int'l v. Lowenschuss, 67 F.3d 1394 (9th Cir. 1995)). So the strike is correct and essentially unwinnable; Purdue did not decide opt-out consent, which remains contested, so the retained opt-out in redline 8.2(a) is itself vulnerable and the Debtor should consider opt-in or voted-yes-only. Exculpation (10.3) should be conformed to the Ninth Circuit limit (Blixseth v. Credit Suisse, 961 F.3d 1074 (9th Cir. 2020): estate fiduciaries and court-appointed parties only; verify), including removal of non-fiduciary Exculpated Parties.

4. EMAIL vs. REDLINE
The email calls most changes cosmetic and omits: the Committee veto over waiving 9.1(g), trustee control, extension of avoidance proceeds to all Avoidance Actions, injunction/discharge carve-outs, the Person/voting edits and Exhibit C date/value changes. Its section cites (6.4, 8.2, 5.3(b)) match neither the redline nor the filed Plan. It lists 11.9 as open-ended while the redline comment calls it non-negotiable; the redline calls $28M a minimum while the email calls it firm.

5. RECOMMENDED RESPONSE AND OPEN ITEMS
1) Request a clean machine compare against the filed Plan and the Committee's Exhibit C source; reject all Exhibit C edits pending contract verification.
2) Concede: release strike; recap claim preservation (narrowed, independent funded trust); supplemental disclosure (no Committee waiver veto; address at DS hearing).
3) Hold: rejection standard; 11.9; trustee selection (tie to funding); board (trade).
4) Counter on economics: financial model from Pinecrest showing max Effective Date payment within $5.15M cushion (about $14.5M pool payment at most before DIP/exit financing, with $9.35M already planned), larger deferred tranche with exit-facility support or secured note, interest at proper 1961 rate; avoidance proceeds share in lieu of a higher pool.
5) Equity: recompute Timberline allocation fully diluted; designate recipients of residual equity; fix $35M circularity; add retention bonuses and DIP to sources and uses.
6) Prepare 503(c) evidence and a correction to DS (class numbering, trustee selection, conditions) before June 12; exchange position papers by May 26; meet-and-confer May 28.
7) Open: DIP balance; exit facility terms; Timberline affiliation with dividend recipients; source of Clearview report; verify ORS, Pomona Valley, Blixseth.
